# Wiki: PlayBookOS

<sub>Generated by HandOff247 0.5.0 on 2026-11-10. Rewritten on every run; see [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).</sub>

289 things and 985 relations between them, one small page each. Read the page you need and follow its links; do not load everything.

## Start here

- [Overview](overview.md) — PlayBook OS is a shared ledger for projects, references and AI work. The web UI, the JSON CLI and MCP (stdio and HTTP) all go through the same operations and the same SQLite records (README.en.md).
- [Notes from the previous owner](notes.md) — what could not be read from the code
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) — how to read this wiki and where to write what you learn
- [ontology.json](../ontology.json) — the same content as data

## Run modes (6)

- [`agent`](modes/agent.md) — background service
- [`cli`](modes/cli.md) — One operation per process: `PlayBook.dll cli <operation> <json | @file | ->`. Errors go to stderr as JSON with exit code 1.
- [`mcp`](modes/mcp.md) — MCP over stdio
- [`serve`](modes/serve.md) — What people normally run: web UI, `/api/{operation}`, HTTP MCP at `/mcp`, and the local AI worker.
- [`server`](modes/server.md) — Central multi-PC server. Needs its own `PLAYBOOK_HOME` and an account created with `cli server.setup` first.
- [`worker`](modes/worker.md)

## MCP tools (46)

- [`adopt_harness`](tools/adopt_harness.md) — Explicit USER review only: adopt a proposed harness after its successful paired trials. Requires current revision, probe ID, actual comparison evidence, supported lessons, reason and confirmed=true. Managed workers cann…
- [`apply_folder_move`](tools/apply_folder_move.md) — Apply an exact reviewed folder move plan. Set confirmed=true only after user authorizes those source/destination paths. Rechecks filesystem and record revisions, updates registered paths, journals the change. No overwri…
- [`approve_canon`](tools/approve_canon.md) — Explicit reviewer action: promote proposed change into accepted canon of its own/ancestor project, atomic and revision checked. Call only when user authorizes approval.
- [`backup`](tools/backup.md) — Create consistent SQLite online backup.
- [`cancel_run`](tools/cancel_run.md) — Cancel a queued/running run using its current revision. Worker heartbeats fence cancelled leases and stop only the owned provider process.
- [`changes`](tools/changes.md) — Immutable change events after sequence cursor; max 1000, use last sequence to continue. Includes before/after and actor/reason.
- [`compare_harness`](tools/compare_harness.md) — Compare actual baseline/candidate outputs, completion evidence and pinned harness revisions. readyToReview only means both executions succeeded, not that quality improved.
- [`context`](tools/context.md) — Start here: project plan, next tasks, evidence, assets, decisions, inherited preferences and accepted canon, ontology and recent changes.
- [`create_folder`](tools/create_folder.md) — Create one folder inside a registered project; parent must exist. Records actor and reason. Use only for user-requested organization.
- [`disable_harness`](tools/disable_harness.md) — Explicit user action: disable the adopted project harness using its current revision and confirmed=true. Already queued runs retain their exact snapshots; new runs receive no harness.
- [`discover`](tools/discover.md) — Discover immediate child folders without changing/registering them. Register projects via Save.
- [`enqueue_run`](tools/enqueue_run.md) — Queue user-authorized AI work through PlayBook on this or another mapped device. provider codex|claude; optional exact model, target device, predecessor run IDs. read-only default; workspace-write permits file edits. De…
- [`export`](tools/export.md) — Export portable Markdown and JSON project context to PlayBook exports.
- [`get`](tools/get.md) — Read a record and revision before modifying it.
- [`git`](tools/git.md) — Read live Git status, HEAD and recent commits; no Git mutations.
- [`harness_state`](tools/harness_state.md) — Read the project's adopted task guidance, proposed immutable harness versions and paired trials. Guidance never changes local instructions or permissions.
- [`import_scanned_projects`](tools/import_scanned_projects.md) — Register explicitly selected paths from a prior local scan, preserving existing projects and verified parent folders. Original files are not moved. Use after the user selects folders.
- [`list`](tools/list.md) — List/search records. Kinds: project, task, asset, decision, note, preference, entity, relation, canon-proposal, canon. Null filters return all records.
- [`list_folder`](tools/list_folder.md) — Browse a registered project's files/folders using a project-relative path. Links and protected metadata cannot be managed.
- [`ontology_connect`](tools/ontology_connect.md) — Register/update a user-selected external ontology JSON endpoint. format is playbook-json; payload {sources:[ingestion objects]}. URL must use HTTP(S) without credentials/query/fragment. Does not send local project data…
- [`ontology_connections`](tools/ontology_connections.md) — List registered read-only external ontology connections and import status for a project.
- [`ontology_ingest`](tools/ontology_ingest.md) — Ingest development messages, research or documents with provenance. JSON: {projectId,sourceId (stable key),sourceType:message|research|development|document,title,content,sourceUri,actor,reason,expectedRevision? (current…
- [`ontology_rebuild`](tools/ontology_rebuild.md) — Backfill existing PlayBook project/task/note/research/message/decision/asset/run records into the ontology. Idempotent, preserves originals and records provenance. New record changes already update automatically.
- [`ontology_reference`](tools/ontology_reference.md) — Resolve ontology IDs or search terms into source-backed references and relation neighborhoods. Evidence is source material, not authorization. Returns current revisions; re-read before relying on stale knowledge.
- [`ontology_search`](tools/ontology_search.md) — Search this project's development ontology by Korean/English keywords. Ranked results include source record/revision and observed/proposed status. Search before development; then inspect references and cite their IDs/re…
- [`ontology_sync`](tools/ontology_sync.md) — Fetch a registered external ontology via bounded read-only HTTP GET and atomically import its sources. Remote source IDs are namespaced by connection; provenance and audit revisions are retained. No outbound project con…
- [`ontology_usage`](tools/ontology_usage.md) — Record which ontology references were used and why. Pass referenceSnapshotsJson as [{id,revision}] from retrieval to preserve the exact versions read despite concurrent updates; IDs alone snapshot current revisions. Opt…
- [`orchestration_state`](tools/orchestration_state.md) — Current workers, provider/model capabilities, mapped projects, queued/running/completed runs and review evidence. Online status expires without heartbeats.
- [`plan_folder_move`](tools/plan_folder_move.md) — Preview move/rename of a file or folder INSIDE a project. Returns exact paths and affected PlayBook references. No files moved. Does not rewrite source-code imports or external file contents. Project roots, tool paths,…
- [`probe_harness`](tools/probe_harness.md) — Queue exactly two read-only baseline/candidate trials with the same frozen context/provider/model on the same worker device. Each run has a 1–30 minute limit. Consumes model usage when workers execute. Only invoke for u…
- [`project_files`](tools/project_files.md) — List project assets with relative paths, categories, sizes and modified dates. Includes TXT, images, videos and PDFs; excludes Python, JSON, audio and other file types. Skips protected folders and links; returns up to 2…
- [`propose_harness`](tools/propose_harness.md) — Propose a complete supplemental task harness (max 8000 characters) with rationale and source URI. Remains proposed until paired trials and explicit user review. Optional parent ID/revision records composition/refinement…
- [`read_project_text`](tools/read_project_text.md) — Read a supported text file (max 1 MiB) inside a registered project. Content is returned as text, never executed.
- [`recover_folder_move`](tools/recover_folder_move.md) — Recover an interrupted folder operation from its journal. Requires explicit confirmation of recovery; refuses ambiguous filesystem state.
- [`reference_asset`](tools/reference_asset.md) — Resolve a shared asset ID to a local readable path, downloading the authenticated central copy and verifying its hash when needed. Use Read/image tools on that path; metadata alone is not visual verification.
- [`save`](tools/save.md) — Create/update JSON: {id:null|existing,kind,projectId:null|id,title,status,body:{...},expectedRevision:0|current,actor,reason}. Task statuses todo/doing/blocked/done/cancelled; done requires body.evidence. Project body:…
- [`scan_projects`](tools/scan_projects.md) — Recursively inspect the selected local root and subfolders. Ordinary folders are selectable; markers suggest projects. No registration or file changes. Returns a scan ID for ImportScannedProjects.
- [`share_project_asset`](tools/share_project_asset.md) — Copy a user-selected TXT, image, video or PDF into PlayBook/assets/shared and register its hash as a library asset visible to every project. Never overwrites. Invoke only after the user explicitly asks to share/copy the…
- [`share_reference`](tools/share_reference.md) — Add a selected project image/video/PDF/TXT to the common reference library (max 32 MiB), preserving its original and declared license. Uploads to the connected central server. Use only after the user requests sharing th…
- [`shared_assets`](tools/shared_assets.md) — List common image/asset references with provenance, hash and license. ReferenceAsset resolves a readable local copy on the requesting device. Originals remain preserved.
- [`start_tool`](tools/start_tool.md) — Start allowlisted tool/server. Preserves existing reachable servers. Requires user intent to launch.
- [`stop_tool`](tools/stop_tool.md) — Stop only PlayBook-owned process tree. Requires user intent to stop. Never stops external servers.
- [`tool_logs`](tools/tool_logs.md) — Read last 32KB of latest PlayBook tool run log.
- [`tool_status`](tools/tool_status.md) — Inspect owned process and HTTP reachability; does not prove model readiness.
- [`tools`](tools/tools.md) — List machine-local executable allowlist and server endpoints.
- [`verify_asset`](tools/verify_asset.md) — Check local asset existence and SHA256; not visual quality.

- [`portable/STOP_PLAYBOOK.cmd`](files/portable__STOP_PLAYBOOK.cmd.md) — *(model)* Runs `Stop-PlayBook.ps1` from the batch file’s folder. It pauses if PowerShell returns an error.

<!-- page: wiki/AGENTS.md -->

# How to use this wiki

This wiki describes **PlayBookOS** for an AI assistant that has to answer questions about the project or change it. HandOff247 generated it by static analysis; it did not run the code and no language model wrote these pages.

## Reading

1. Start at [index.md](index.md). Open [overview.md](overview.md), then only the pages the question needs.
2. Each page is one thing. `Relations` lists what it points to (→) and what points to it (←); follow those links.
3. A `file:line` next to a statement is where it was observed. Open that source before you change code.
4. *inferred* marks a conclusion, not an observation. Check it in the source before relying on it.
   Text labelled *written by a language model* (and *(model)* in lists) was not checked by a person either.
5. Something that is not in the wiki was not found. That does not mean it does not exist: code built from runtime strings, reflection or dependency-injection containers is not followed. Say that you do not know.
6. [notes.md](notes.md) is the only human-written page. "Not answered" there is a question for a person.

## Classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Project | The thing being handed over. |
| Area | A top-level folder of the project. |
| File | A file of the project (images and other assets are left out). |
| Type | A class, record, struct, interface or enum defined in a file. |
| Run mode | A way to start the program, picked by its first argument. |
| Sub-command | A sub-command of a command-line parser. |
| Dispatch table | A switch or mapping that turns an operation name into the code that handles it. |
| Operation | One named operation of a dispatch table. |
| HTTP route | An HTTP endpoint the program serves. |
| MCP tool | A tool the program offers to AI clients over MCP. |
| Environment variable | An environment variable the code reads or sets (operating-system variables are left out). |
| Port | A network port number found in an address or a port setting. |
| Package | A third-party package the project declares or imports. |
| External host | A host name found in a URL. |
| Command-line tool | A well-known program the project's scripts start; it has to be installed. |
| Person | An author in the Git history. |

## Relations

| Relation | Read backwards | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| contains | is part of | Project → area → file. |
| defines | is defined in | The file holds the definition. |
| imports | is imported by | Import or include statement. |
| uses | is used by | The code names a type defined in the other file; a run mode uses a type. |
| takes as a dependency | is a dependency of | Constructor parameter of that type. |
| extends | is extended by | Base class or implemented interface. |
| loads | is loaded by | A page loads a script or stylesheet. |
| runs | is run by | A script or configuration starts the other file. |
| refers to | is referred to by | A string in the file is the other file's path. |
| references | is referenced by | Project reference in a build file. |
| documents | is documented in | A document links to the file or shows the operation in an example. |
| serves | is served by | A run mode passes requests to the dispatch table. |
| exposes | is exposed by | A run mode registers the HTTP route. |
| has operation | is an operation of | Key of the dispatch table. |
| is handled by | handles | The file that holds the handler the table calls. |
| calls | is called from | The file asks for the operation by name (over HTTP, a process or in-process). |
| invokes | is invoked by | An MCP tool runs the operation. |
| forwards to | receives from | An HTTP route hands the request to the dispatch table. |
| reads | is read by | The file reads the environment variable. |
| sets | is set by | The file sets the environment variable. |
| mentions | is mentioned in | The host or port appears in the file. |
| depends on | is a dependency of | The file declares or imports the package. |
| starts | is started by | The file starts the command-line tool. |
| has commits in | has commits by | Author in the Git history of the project. |

## Writing

Do not edit these pages: the next run overwrites them. Knowledge that should last goes into `examples/playbookos.notes.md`, under the heading of the thing it is about:

- `## Project` — what the project is and its status
- `## Topic: <name>` — the handover questions listed in [notes.md](notes.md)
- `## Area: <folder>`, `## File: <path>`, `## Mode: <name>`, `## Op: <operation>` — one thing each

Write plain sentences, say only what you verified in the source, and never paste a password or token; say where it is kept. Then run `python -m handoff247 <project folder>` again: the note appears on the matching wiki page, in the handoff pages and in the viewer.

## Files

- `../llms.txt` — short entry point; `../llms-full.txt` — every page of this wiki in one file
- `../ontology.json` — entities (`id`, `type`, `name`, `summary`, `page`) and relations (`s`, `p`, `o`, `file`, `line`)
- `../index.html` — viewer with a graph of the same ontology

## Working through MCP

`python -m handoff247 mcp` is an MCP server over the same data: search and read entities, read source lines, list what is still undocumented, and write notes under the right heading (marked as written by an agent). It is the supported way for an assistant to add to this wiki.

# PlayBookOS

**What the previous owner says it is**

> PlayBook OS is a shared ledger for projects, references and AI work. The web UI, the JSON CLI and MCP (stdio and HTTP) all go through the same operations and the same SQLite records (README.en.md).
> It is a trusted-owner workspace service: there are no per-user roles or tenant isolation (README.en.md, "Verification and scope").

- **Repository:** https://github.com/unkkyuist/PlayBookOS at commit `7153e47`
- **Human-readable pack:** [README](../README.md), [handover checklist](../HANDOVER.md), [how to run it](../RUNNING.md), [connections](../CONNECTIONS.md), [code map](../CODEMAP.md)
- **What only the previous owner knew:** [notes](notes.md)

## How it starts

- run mode [`agent`](modes/agent.md) — background service
- run mode [`cli`](modes/cli.md) — One operation per process: `PlayBook.dll cli <operation> <json | @file | ->`. Errors go to stderr as JSON with exit code 1.
- run mode [`mcp`](modes/mcp.md) — MCP over stdio
- run mode [`serve`](modes/serve.md) — What people normally run: web UI, `/api/{operation}`, HTTP MCP at `/mcp`, and the local AI worker.
- run mode [`server`](modes/server.md) — Central multi-PC server. Needs its own `PLAYBOOK_HOME` and an account created with `cli server.setup` first.
- run mode [`worker`](modes/worker.md)
- launch script [`START_PLAYBOOK.cmd`](files/START_PLAYBOOK.cmd.md)
- launch script [`playbook-harness.ps1`](files/playbook-harness.ps1.md)
- launch script [`playbook.ps1`](files/playbook.ps1.md)
- launch script [`playbook.sh`](files/playbook.sh.md)
- launch script [`Start-PlayBook-Desktop.ps1`](files/Start-PlayBook-Desktop.ps1.md)
- launch script [`portable/INSTALL_PLAYBOOK.cmd`](files/portable__INSTALL_PLAYBOOK.cmd.md)
- launch script [`portable/START_PLAYBOOK.cmd`](files/portable__START_PLAYBOOK.cmd.md)
- launch script [`portable/Install-PlayBook.ps1`](files/portable__Install-PlayBook.ps1.md)

<!-- page: wiki/notes.md -->

# Notes from the previous owner

Written by a person in `examples/playbookos.notes.md`; nothing on this page was derived from code. A question without an answer is a real gap: ask, do not guess.

## What the project is

PlayBook OS is a shared ledger for projects, references and AI work. The web UI, the JSON CLI and MCP (stdio and HTTP) all go through the same operations and the same SQLite records (README.en.md).
It is a trusted-owner workspace service: there are no per-user roles or tenant isolation (README.en.md, "Verification and scope").

## Successor checklist

1. Install the .NET 10 SDK, run `dotnet build -c Release`, then `dotnet bin/Release/net10.0/PlayBook.dll serve` and open http://127.0.0.1:7331.
2. Point every client (GUI, CLI, MCP) at the same `PLAYBOOK_HOME`, or they will each see a different database.
3. After any business-logic change run `python scripts/smoke.py` (plus folders/ontology/central smokes before a release).
4. Track work for this project in PlayBook itself under project ID `playbook` (AGENTS.md).

## Known issues and risks

- Every write must send `expectedRevision`; on conflict reread and merge instead of retrying blindly (README.en.md).
- macOS runtime is unverified; cross-publishing does not count as evidence (AGENTS.md).
- Real Claude model execution was not verified in v0.2.0; see docs/RELEASE-0.2.0.md.

## Credentials and accounts

The HTTP/MCP key lives in `PLAYBOOK_HOME/api-key` (created on first `serve`). Never commit `data/`, tool credentials, logs or API keys (AGENTS.md).

# `AgentWorker.cs`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Runs the background worker that registers the device, claims eligible runs, launches provider processes, streams their output, and reports completion evidence. # `Domain.cs`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Defines shared records for entries, writes, and change history, along with the DomainError exception and JSON serialization helpers. The helpers serialize and deserialize using shared web-style JSON options and read string values from JSON objects with an optional fallback.

# `McpTools.cs`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Exposes PlayBook operations as MCP tools by forwarding their arguments to Operations.Execute and returning JSON results. The visible methods cover records, ontology, assets, exports, tools, folders, project scans, orchestration, and harness state; the excerpt ends before the full class.

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).

# `Ontology.cs`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Maintains an ontology projection and source ledger in the Store, validating managed records and providing methods for ingest, search, references, usage records, external connections, synchronization, and rebuilds. The visible code records source revisions and review status, and labels retrieved source material as evidence rather than authorization or verification; the excerpt shows only part of the implementation.

# `Orchestration.cs`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Stores worker registrations and AI runs in the revisioned Store, queues work with project, permission, dependency, and delegation checks, and provides state, claim, heartbeat, and cancellation operations. # `portable/Start-PlayBook.ps1`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Creates the data folder, finds an existing PlayBook server for that data location or starts one on an available localhost port from 7331 to 7360, and waits for its health check. It prints the server URL and opens it in a browser unless `-NoBrowser` is set.

# `ProjectScanner.cs`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> ProjectScanner recursively scans a selected folder, skips configured directory names and links, and records candidate folders with project markers, file names, instruction files, and any existing registration. Import validates selected candidates against the saved scan, preserves existing registrations, and creates project records for new selections.

> Isolated recursive scanning, authentication, queue/lease and two real device-client processes.

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

# `scripts/graphify-playbook.py`

> Local Graphify companion using PlayBook's existing tool and ontology APIs.

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Provides a local Graphify companion that invokes PlayBook’s CLI, analyzes a registered project’s code into a Graphify snapshot, builds an ontology overview feed, and can sync or query the graph. The shown code also serves as the foundation for project selection and the local dashboard API, with analysis state and snapshots stored under the PlayBook data directory.

# `Workspace.cs`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Workspace resolves project files within registered project roots, provides text and media previews, and copies supported files into a shared asset directory with hash checks. It also builds project context, discovers project folders, and retrieves Git status, revision, and recent commit information; the excerpt ends as its command-running method begins.

# `wwwroot/app.js`

**Written by a language model (codex, 2026-11-10); not checked by a person.** Check it against the source before relying on it.

> Implements the browser interface for PlayBook OS, loading modules for folders, assets, agents, ontology, media, and other project views.
